subject: Intermittent throughput affecting token generation for NovaCorp — situational update
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [SEV2] Spike in model token latency impacting NovaCorp requests

Team,

We detected an intermittent throughput regression for the model variant serving NovaCorp's production region starting ~08:50 PDT. Error rates are low but median token generation latency has jumped ~4x for about 15-25% of requests. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/stream for model-redwood-003-quant.

What we've done so far:
- Identified a pattern: latency correlates with longer context windows (>2.5k tokens) and a subset of hosts reporting memory pressure.
- Collected kernel-level traces and KV-cache hop counts (attached).
- Scoped impact: NovaCorp traffic constitutes ~12% of requests in the affected pool; other customers see minimal impact.

Immediate asks:
- Mina: can you notify the NovaCorp POC with an initial acknowledgment and ETA for a fuller update?
- Karthik & Iyer: please prioritize a remediation path (kernel fallback or scale burst) and estimate timeline.
- Monica: loop CS/AM for customer comms and potential SLA credit discussion.

Attachments: harvest_runtime-logs-20270610.txt (traces), telemetry-snapshot-20270610.json

I'll stand up a short bridge if needed. Planning to escalate to SEV-1 if error rates exceed 3% or degradation persists beyond 3 hours.

Marcus
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@novacorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:35:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent throughput affecting NovaCorp — situational update

Dana,

Thanks for flagging this with your team. We're aware of intermittent increased latency affecting a subset of NovaCorp requests to our generation endpoints. We are actively investigating and have the SRE and runtime teams on it.

What you should know now:
- Impact: Some longer-context requests are returning tokens slower than normal; functionality is intact.
- Scope: ~12% of NovaCorp request volume; we have mitigations ready if the impact expands.
- ETA for next update: 60 minutes (we'll provide an update even sooner if root cause becomes clear).

Immediate mitigations being worked right now:
- Automated traffic routing to warm hosts tolerant of higher context lengths.
- Kernel fallback to a conservative scheduling path where we see memory pressure.

We are treating this as a priority. Monica (CC'd) is your customer success lead and will track communications and credits. Marcus and Karthik are investigating and will provide technical details for the postmortem.

Attachments: telemetry-snapshot-20270610.json (current metrics sample)

Apologies for the disruption — I know this impacts your production usage. I will follow up with a technical update in the next hour and an executive summary once we have a durable mitigation.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@novacorp.com>

Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 13:08:17 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent throughput affecting NovaCorp — situational update

Mina,

Thanks for the prompt acknowledgment. We saw the latency surface in our observability around 08:45 PDT and it has been affecting time-to-first-token for our user-facing endpoints. Our SRE (Evan) is on standby and has asked for escalation to leadership if you expect >2 hours to mitigation.

Request: please include a brief executive summary for our CTO (Evan) and any proposed remediation options and timelines in your next update. Also confirm whether this incident will be included in the monthly SLA report.

Appreciate the quick coordination — looking forward to your update.

Dana Liu
Head of Product Operations, NovaCorp
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@novacorp.com>, Evan Park <e.park@novacorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: NovaCorp incident update — mitigation in place, next steps and postmortem plan

Dana, Evan,

This is an executive-facing summary following our operational updates. Thank you for your patience while we investigated. Below is a concise summary, current state, and the plan for remediation and follow-up.

Summary of impact:
- Start: 2027-06-10 08:50 PDT.
- Visible effect: increased token generation latency for ~12% of NovaCorp requests, mainly for contexts >2.5k tokens. No data loss or corruption; requests complete successfully but slower.

Root cause (interim):
- Our telemetry shows a memory-pressure pattern on a subset of inference hosts running the quantized model kernel. Under longer contexts the scheduler was triggering a fallback path that increased per-token CPU scheduling overhead. We are classifying this as a multi-factor regression: a kernel scheduler sensitivity + uneven warm pool distribution.

Mitigation applied (completed 2027-06-11 13:40 PDT):
- Immediately rerouted NovaCorp traffic to warm hosts with verified KV-cache compatibility.
- Deployed a temporary kernel scheduler patch that disables the pathological fallback for the affected hosts.
- Triggered a controlled ramp of additional instances in the dedicated pool to reduce per-host load.

Current status:
- Observed median token latency returned to baseline within ~20 minutes of routing change. A small subset of long-context requests may still see transient delays; we've reduced those to <1% of NovaCorp volume.

Customer impact & compensation:
- Functionality restored; performance degradation window: ~08:50 PDT (Jun 10) to ~13:40 PDT (Jun 11) for a subset of requests.
- Monica will follow up on SLA credit calculations and a formal incident report for your records.

Follow-up and postmortem plan:
- We will publish a detailed postmortem with timeline, root cause analysis, and permanent remediation steps by 2027-06-18. Link will be shared to your team (Drive link below).
- Action items for Redwood:
  1) Permanent kernel scheduler fix and regression test coverage for long-context workloads.
  2) Improve warm-pool distribution heuristics to avoid skew.
  3) Add a custom NovaCorp routing policy (optional) to reduce blast radius for high-context requests.

Links & artifacts:
- PagerDuty incident: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/RI-1427
- Postmortem folder (will contain final report): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B-incident-novacorp-postmortem
- Diagnostic attachments (already shared): harvest_runtime-logs-20270610.txt, telemetry-snapshot-20270610.json

Next steps:
- Monica will schedule a 30-min review with your engineering leadership for 2027-06-15 (proposed).
- I'll send the postmortem draft by 2027-06-17 for your review.

If you need anything sooner, please ping me directly. We value NovaCorp’s partnership and apologize for the service disruption.

Best regards,
Mina Haddad
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
